summary: Announces an April 1972 workshop at MIT to revise the Data Transfer and File Transfer Protocols from RFCs 264 and 265 into a unified convention, considering the needs of TIP users, datacomputer users and remote job entry.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC announces a workshop at MIT to discuss revisions to ARPANET data and file transfer protocols. The goal is to work toward a common approach that considers several kinds of network users.

subtitle: An announcement for a workshop on revising ARPANET data and file transfer protocols.

tldr.problem: The RFC says participants wanted to revise the existing data and file transfer protocols to suit better-understood ARPANET needs.
tldr.mechanism: MIT planned a two-day workshop with talks and working sessions on protocol changes and a possible unified convention.
tldr.outcome: Attendance was by invitation, with interested people asked to contact the organizer; participants were encouraged to prepare position papers.

sections.title: Workshop Purpose
sections.content:
MIT will host a data and file transfer workshop on April 14 and 15, 1972. The announcement says people had expressed interest in revising RFCs 264 and 265 to better meet current ARPANET requirements.

The workshop's objective is to arrive at a unified convention while considering TIP users, datacomputer users, remote job entry users and major network service systems.
sections.plainLanguage: The organizers want to review the separate data and file transfer protocols. They hope to agree on a common approach that works for different users and services.

sections.title: Agenda and Participants
sections.content:
The Friday agenda includes talks about the datacomputer, data and file transfer to Terminal IMPs, remote job service from server and user viewpoints, TENEX file copying, and measurements. Friday and Saturday sessions include group discussions and working time on revised protocol specifications.

The announcement limits attendance to invitees but asks people who want to attend to contact Abhay Bhushan. It encourages participants to prepare written position papers in advance.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants will hear several site and user perspectives, then discuss revisions together. Interested people can contact the organizer to request attendance.

sections.title: Topics for Discussion
sections.content:
Data Transfer Protocol topics include its relationship to TELNET, error control and recovery, transfer modes, information separators and use with TIPs and the datacomputer.

File Transfer Protocol topics include ICP, mixing data and control, command language, data types and physical storage, descriptors and logical structure, error recovery, TIP and datacomputer use, and uniform pathnames for a possible ARPANET virtual file system.
sections.plainLanguage: The agenda covers how to detect errors, represent data and transfer files. It also asks how the protocols should work with TIPs and the datacomputer.
